text.p: Italy's debt market ended sharply lower, weighed down by a super-strong dollar and profit-taking, the second consecutive session which saw Btp futures slide more than other European bond markets.
Traders said the main factor was the strength of the dollar, steady above 1.80 marks, which was blurring the future scenario of the single European currency.
"If the mark remains so weak then it raises worries about a tightening of the Bundesbank's policy," one trader said, also citing France's difficulties as another weakening factor for the euro.
Operators said Btps are suffering more than other European bonds because of the market's desire for profits.
"After a month's rally this is more than normal," one said.
In cash bonds, the February 2007 Btp closed 57 basis points easier at 101.98, yielding 6.56 percent. The 10-year Btp/Bund spread widened to 93/94 bps against 91 bps at Monday's close.
